current_example.title: Example: Determining Components of a Vector Orthogonal to Two Given Vectors

q-74089.name: Question 1
q-74089.problem:
Given the vector $u=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$, which of the following vectors are orthogonal to $u?$

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$
q-74089.worked_solution:
We compute the dot product between $u$ and each of the listed vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =2\cdot (-2)+(-1)\cdot 1+3\cdot 0+5\cdot 1 \\  & =-4-1+0+5 \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot w & ={u}_{1}\cdot {w}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {w}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {w}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {w}_{4} \\  & =2\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 4+3\cdot (-1)+5\cdot 1 \\  & =2-4-3+5 \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot x & ={u}_{1}\cdot {x}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {x}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {x}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {x}_{4} \\  & =2\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 0+3\cdot (-2)+5\cdot (-1) \\  & =4+0-6-5 \\  & =-7.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the correct option is $v$ and $w$ only.

q-74089.html:
Question 1
?

Given the vector u=[2−135], which of the following vectors are orthogonal to u? v=[−2101],w=[14−11],x=[20−2−1].

a
v only
b
x only
c
v and w only
d
w only
e
v and x only
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We compute the dot product between u and each of the listed vectors:

u⋅v=u1⋅v1+u2⋅v2+u3⋅v3+u4⋅v4=2⋅(−2)+(−1)⋅1+3⋅0+5⋅1=−4−1+0+5=0.✓

u⋅w=u1⋅w1+u2⋅w2+u3⋅w3+u4⋅w4=2⋅1+(−1)⋅4+3⋅(−1)+5⋅1=2−4−3+5=0.✓

u⋅x=u1⋅x1+u2⋅x2+u3⋅x3+u4⋅x4=2⋅2+(−1)⋅0+3⋅(−2)+5⋅(−1)=4+0−6−5=−7.×

Consequently, the correct option is v and w only.

q-74086.name: Question 2
q-74086.problem:
Given the vector $u=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$, which of the following vectors are orthogonal to $u?$

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$
q-74086.worked_solution:
We compute the dot product between $u$ and each of the listed vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =3\cdot (-1)+0\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot 1+1\cdot 2 \\  & =-3+0-1+2 \\  & =-2.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot w & ={u}_{1}\cdot {w}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {w}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {w}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {w}_{4} \\  & =3\cdot 1+0\cdot 3+(-1)\cdot 1+1\cdot (-2) \\  & =3+0-1-2 \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot x & ={u}_{1}\cdot {x}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {x}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {x}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {x}_{4} \\  & =3\cdot 2+0\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 2+1\cdot (-4) \\  & =6+0-2-4 \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the correct option is $w$ and $x$ only.

q-39319.name: Question 3
q-39319.problem: If $u=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ k \\ 2 \\ -6\end{aligned}]$ and $v=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ -8 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal vectors, then $k=$
q-39319.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that their dot product is equal to zero.
First, let's calculate the dot product in terms of $k$:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =(-5)\cdot (-3)+k\cdot (-1)+2\cdot (-8)+(-6)\cdot 1 \\  & =15-k-16-6 \\  & =-k-7\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the dot product to zero, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-k-7 & =0 \\ k & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

q-74093.name: Question 4
q-74093.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}k \\ -3 \\ 1 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -3 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $a⊥b.$ Find the value of $k.$
q-74093.worked_solution:
Since $a$ and $b$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that their dot product is equal to zero.
First, let's calculate the dot product in terms of $k$:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{1}\cdot {b}_{1}+{a}_{2}\cdot {b}_{2}+{a}_{3}\cdot {b}_{3}+{a}_{4}\cdot {b}_{4} \\  & =k\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot (-1)+1\cdot (-3)+k\cdot k \\  & =2k+3-3+{k}^{2} \\  & =2k+{k}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the dot product to zero, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2k+{k}^{2} & =0 \\ k(2+k) & =0 \\ k & =-2,0.\end{aligned}
$$

q-39293.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ a \\ 7 \\ b\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 0 \\ -6\end{aligned}],$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $u$ is orthogonal to $v$ and $w.$ What is the value of $a+b?$
q-39293.worked_solution:
Given that $u$ is orthogonal to $v$ and $w$, we have

$$
\{\begin{aligned}u\cdot v=0 \\ u\cdot w=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's consider the first equation $u\cdot v=0.$ Calculating the dot product in terms of $a$ and $b$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & =0 \\ 2\cdot 1+a\cdot 4+7\cdot 0+b\cdot (-6) & =0 \\ 2+4a-6b & =0 \\ 4a-6b & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, for the second equation $u\cdot w=0$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot w & =0 \\ 2\cdot (-4)+a\cdot 3+7\cdot 5+b\cdot 4 & =0 \\ -8+3a+35+4b & =0 \\ 3a+4b & =-27.\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the values of $a$ and $b$, we need to solve the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4a-6b=-2 \\ 3a+4b=-27.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $-3,$ the second equation by $4,$ and adding the resulting equations, we obtain

$$
34b=-102\,⟹\,b=-3.
$$

Substituting $b=-3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4a-6(-3) & =-2 \\ 4a+18 & =-2 \\ 4a & =-20 \\ a & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have that

$$
a+b=-5+(-3)=-8.
$$

So, to find the values of $a$ and $b$, we need to solve the system

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}4a+b=13 \\ a-3b=-13\end{aligned}\end{aligned}

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(2)+b & =13 \\ 8+b & =13 \\ b & =5.\end{aligned}

Finally, we have that

$$
a+b=2+5=7.
